title: batch-sherpa-queue-rebalance-and-kv-softpin-smoothing
author: Priya Desai
description:
Motivation: We observe intermittent tail-latency spikes in mixed-priority traffic where short low-cost requests get starved by long-running KV-heavy cohorts during continuous batching. This PR introduces a lightweight scheduling heuristic ("Batch Sherpa") that rebalances queue leases across cohorts, applies a soft-pin strategy for KV-cache hot keys, and smooths per-cohort fairness scores over time to avoid oscillation and thrashing.

Design summary: Batch Sherpa operates at the scheduler's lease rebalancer stage. Key ideas: 1) Cohort rebalancing: periodically (configurable window) compute a cohesion score per queue based on recent service time, queue growth, and SLA misses; queues with high cohesion but low service get short lease bonuses, while abusive cohorts get lease decrements. 2) Fairness smoothing: maintain an exponentially weighted fairness score (alpha default 0.08) to avoid large step changes when traffic mixes shift. 3) KV soft-pin: identify hot KV keys based on access frequency and allow soft pinning in the local KV cache with TTL extension heuristics that decay if eviction pressure rises. Soft-pin does not prevent eviction in extreme memory pressure; it only biases cache retention and reporting for the scheduler to avoid pin-related starvation. 4) Adaptive timeout backoff: when queue horizons indicate persistent timeouts, timeouts backoff incrementally by cohort to reduce retries and queue thrashing.

Behavioral changes and flags: All features are gated behind runtime-config flags: scheduler.batch_sherpa.enabled (default: true on canary, false on main rollout), scheduler.batch_sherpa.alpha (fairness smoothing), kv.soft_pin.enabled (default: true), kv.soft_pin.max_ttl_ms (default: 120000). Defaults are conservative; the rollout plan disables Batch Sherpa on regions with <2 p99 violations in 24h.

Files changed (high level): list below contains small illustrative snippets and intended effect. No user-facing API changes.

Benchmarks & results: Running the mixed-priority benchmark harness (see perf/bench/batcher_mixed_priority.yaml) on a 4xA100 instance: baseline median latency: 32ms, p99: 1.9s. With Batch Sherpa (canary parameters): median: 30ms (-6%), p99: 1.05s (-45%). KV-heavy synthetic scenario (50% long KV ops) saw p90 reduce by 27% and p99 by 40% under sustained load. CPU overhead: scheduler CPU increased by ~2% in steady state; memory footprint increased modestly due to soft-pin metadata (~2-6MB per server).

Compatibility: The heuristic is compatible with existing lease/rebalancer contracts; it only touches scheduler decision surface and KV cache retention policy. Rollback is safe via flags and feature toggle.

Testing: Added unit tests around lease rebalancer invariants and fairness smoothing, plus an integration test reproducing starvation under sustained KV-heavy cohorts (tests/integration/batcher_starvation_test.go). Metrics added to observe: batcher.sherpa.rebalances, batcher.sherpa.fairness_score, kv.soft_pin.hits, kv.soft_pin.evictions.

Rollout plan: 1) Canary in dedicated and hosted canaries (1% of traffic) for 48h; 2) monitor newly added metrics and existing p99/p999 dashboards; 3) enable for 25% traffic for 72h; 4) full roll when no regressions. Auto-rollback if p99 increases >10% for 3 consecutive windows.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration starvation test
- [x] Benchmarks recorded and uploaded to perf lab
- [x] Console toggles wired for operations
- [x] Documentation draft (docs/scheduler/batch-sherpa.md)

Related work: This PR complements previous work that introduced lease probing and cohort deadlines (see ENG-3821 and pr references). It intentionally avoids strict priority queueing to keep throughput high for best-effort workloads.

Notes: The code includes a small deterministic seed used in rebalancer sampling; this is intentionally bounded to keep experiments reproducible. If this PR uncovers cases where soft-pin causes cache churn, we will flip default to off and iterate on eviction heuristics.

release_notes: Added Batch Sherpa scheduling heuristic to reduce batching-induced tail latency, plus KV cache soft-pin to preserve hot key locality. Controlled rollout behind feature flags; see docs/scheduler/batch-sherpa.md for operational guidance.
